sub_fixes_applied.summary: Replaced the unconditional thinking:false / thinkingAt:0 reset in the fetchSessions decrypt loop with conservative preserve-if-recent logic. Reads existingSession from storage.getState().sessions[session.id]; if existingSession.thinking === true AND server's session.activeAt is within the last 5000ms, preserves thinking:true / thinkingAt from the existing record. Otherwise resets to false/0 (preserves prior behaviour). storage was already imported at line 6 of sync.ts. Used !! coercion on the boolean expression and the non-null-assertion existingSession! inside the ternary to keep TypeScript happy without changing the conditional logic.

harmonization_notes:
Preserve-if-recent logic (7.3.C) is intentionally conservative and works regardless of pipeline 7.2's behaviour:
  - If 7.2 ships a server thinking-snapshot on connect: snapshot arrives within ~1s of connect; the 5s preserve window bridges that gap, then the snapshot overwrites cleanly (no UI flash).
  - If 7.2 misses or is delayed: 5s preserve gives the CLI's next ~2s session-alive ephemeral time to arrive (CLI heartbeat is volatile.emit every 2s per packages/happy-cli/src/claude/session.ts:69-73).
  - If session is truly idle: server's activeAt is older than 5s, preserveThinking=false, behaviour matches the prior unconditional reset.
A follow-up cycle can tighten the window to <2s once 7.2's behaviour is verified end-to-end; loosening to 10s would also be safe but less responsive on indicator-cleared transitions.

7.3.A and 7.3.B together provide defence-in-depth for the visible-session catch-up:
  - 7.3.A (SessionView.tsx socketStatus dep): fires when a SessionView is mounted and socketStatus transitions. Covers the common 'tab visible during reconnect' case.
  - 7.3.B (sync.ts onReconnected): fires on every reconnect regardless of which component is mounted, IF a session was recently visible. Covers backgrounded-tab and freshly-reopened-window cases.
Neither is strictly necessary if the other is reliable, but ED specs explicitly call this 'redundant safety net'. Cost is 6 lines of executable logic + comments; benefit is robustness against React effect-timing edge cases.
